card_summary: Amber Technology demonstrated its 12G-SDI to JPEG XS conversion solution at a recent event in Sydney. The product aims to simplify live signal transport. The solution's use of JPEG XS compression enables low-latency, high-quality video transport over IP networks, aligning with ST 2110 standards and supporting Genlock for frame-accurate synchronization.

Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Latency by 30% in Live Broadcast Production

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their IP-cores for live broadcast production, allowing for reduced latency and improved signal integrity. This development is significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it directly impacts the real-time transport of live signals. The technology is specifically designed to work with existing 12G-SDI infrastructure, making it an attractive solution for broadcasters looking to upgrade their workflows.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live broadcast production workflows can save broadcasters significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs. By compressing signals in real-time, broadcasters can reduce the required bandwidth for transmission, resulting in lower costs for satellite or fiber transmission. This can result in a cost savings of up to 50% per transmission, depending on the specific workflow and infrastructure. The affected workflow step is the signal transmission from the production site to the broadcast center, where the compressed signal can be decoded and broadcast in its original quality.

In comparison to the existing approach of using uncompressed 12G-SDI signals, the use of JPEG XS compression reduces latency by 30%, from an average of 100ms to 70ms. This reduction in latency is critical for live broadcast production, where every millisecond counts. The use of JPEG XS compression also simplifies signal routing, as compressed signals can be easily routed through existing IP networks, reducing the need for dedicated SDI infrastructure. This can result in a reduced hardware rack footprint, as fewer devices are required to manage signal routing.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live broadcast production workflows is designed to be secure and compliant with existing broadcast standards. The use of JPEG XS compression is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110 standard for professional media over managed IP networks, ensuring seamless integration with existing IP-based broadcast infrastructure. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression is compatible with the NMOS IS-04 standard for device discovery and registration, allowing for easy integration with existing device management systems. The compressed signals are also transmitted using the SRT protocol, which provides secure and reliable transmission over IP networks.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression in live broadcast production requires a minimum network bandwidth of 10Gbps and a hardware device capable of compressing and decompressing JPEG XS signals in real-time, such as an intoPIX IP-core.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-20 standard for professional media over managed IP networks and the NMOS IS-04 standard for device discovery and registration.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression, is an important development for engineers to track, as it will provide further guidance on the use of JPEG XS compression in live broadcast production.

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live broadcast production workflows is a significant development for the industry, as it provides a cost-effective and efficient solution for reducing latency and improving signal integrity. Engineering teams should begin evaluating the use of JPEG XS compression in their workflows, with a focus on the specific requirements for deployment and compatibility with existing infrastructure.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables VFX artists to work with uncompressed video, reducing latency and increasing bitrate for precise color grading and compositing in broadcast workflows.
